While the story is very well-crafted and offers a poignant, nuanced look at human nature—specifically regarding unspoken grief, stoicism, and the quiet ways estranged family members extend olive branches—it does not present a "unique and original idea." Instead, it relies on familiar, universal themes of loss (the death of a husband/father) and tentative reconciliation (offering the deceased father's boots to the son), executing them with emotional depth rather than conceptual novelty.
